blocks.value: Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) measures how efficiently a company uses all of its capital—including shareholders' money and borrowed money—to generate profits.

Imagine This: Two factory owners each invest ₹50 lakh of their own money and borrow another ₹50 lakh from the bank. The owner who earns higher profits from the combined ₹1 crore is using capital more efficiently. ROCE measures this.
Unlike ROE, which focuses only on shareholders' equity, ROCE considers the total capital employed in the business.
Capital-intensive industries such as manufacturing, power and infrastructure often use ROCE as an important performance measure.
Many experienced investors prefer companies that consistently maintain a healthy ROCE over several years.
